walkthroughs.body_html:
Astrophysics — a core area of GCSE Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Astrophysics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Astrophysics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A star with surface temperature twice that of the Sun emits how many times more power per unit area?
Wien's law allows us to determine a star's:
options: Distance
Surface temperature
Mass
Radial velocity

mcqs.q: What produces a magnetic field around a wire?
options: The number of turns in the coil alone.
The voltage across the wire creates magnetism.
A moving electric charge — i.e. an electric current.
The metal in the wire is naturally magnetic.

mcqs.q: According to Faraday's law, what determines the size of the induced emf in a coil?
options: The number of turns in the coil alone.
The rate of change of magnetic flux linkage through the coil.
The voltage across the wire creates magnetism.
The strength of the magnetic field alone.

mcqs.q: What does the spacing of field lines on a diagram indicate?
options: Field lines are equally important regardless of spacing — only the arrows matter.
Wider spacing means a stronger field because the lines have more room to act.
The voltage across the wire creates magnetism.
The strength of the field — closer lines mean a stronger field.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Stefan's law”?
options: Brightness of a star as observed from Earth on a logarithmic scale.
λ_max T = 2.9 × 10⁻³ m K, linking peak wavelength to absolute temperature.
Apparent magnitude a star would have at 10 parsecs: m − M = 5 log(d/10).
Total power emitted by a black body: P = σAT⁴.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Parsec”?
options: Total power emitted by a black body: P = σAT⁴.
Apparent magnitude a star would have at 10 parsecs: m − M = 5 log(d/10).
Brightness of a star as observed from Earth on a logarithmic scale.
Distance at which 1 AU subtends 1 arcsecond, about 3.26 light-years.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Wien's displacement law”?
options: Brightness of a star as observed from Earth on a logarithmic scale.
λ_max T = 2.9 × 10⁻³ m K, linking peak wavelength to absolute temperature.
Plot of luminosity against temperature, classifying stars into main sequence, giants, supergiants, white dwarfs.
Total power emitted by a black body: P = σAT⁴.
